# The Sky That Stretches Beyond Our Sight

## Scripture

*"Can you bind the chains of the Pleiades? Can you loosen Orion's belt? Can you bring forth the constellations in their seasons?"* — Job 38:31–32 (NIV)

## Reflection

On crisp October nights, the constellation Orion climbs above the eastern horizon, its three bright belt stars unmistakable. Yet Orion is only a neighbor—a few hundred light-years away. Beyond it stretches the Milky Way, a river of billions of suns so distant their light has traveled thousands of years to reach us. And beyond that? Galaxies upon galaxies, scattered like seed across a field no one can measure.

When Job questioned God's justice, God answered not with explanations but with questions—questions about binding stars and guiding constellations. The point was never astronomy. The point was this: the God who steadies Orion's belt also holds every trembling heart. If He tends the Pleiades with such care, will He not tend you?

Fall reminds us that seasons change, that light fades earlier, that the year is loosening its grip. But the constellations still appear in their seasons, faithful as clockwork. God's care for you is no less constant. The One who named the stars has not forgotten your name.

## Prayer

Lord of the heavens, when my vision shrinks to the size of my worries, lift my eyes to the skies You spoke into being. Remind me that the God who guides Orion through the darkness also guides me. In every season, in every night, hold me in Your unwavering care. Amen.
